status_note: filed [#25521](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/issues/25521), open (reproduced); reproduces on 2.0.0 and the 2.0.1/2.1.0 nightlies. Main adds an opt-in `parquet_can_have_nan` setting ([#27969](https://github.com/duckdb/duckdb/pull/27969)); the default still trusts the statistics. The wrong `max(x)` is new since 1.5 (1.4.1 gives NaN). The Parquet docs document the `can_have_nan` option (default `false`), with which the reader accounts for NaN in a column's min/max statistics (https://duckdb.org/docs/2.0/data/parquet/overview#parameters): the wrong results under the default are documented behaviour, and the report should cite the option.
summary: `read_parquet` trusts a file's min/max statistics for doubles, which Parquet writers compute without NaN. Comparisons are folded from them and row groups skipped, though DuckDB orders NaN above every double: NaN rows go missing or compare wrongly.
repro: A Parquet file of `x = [0.5, NaN]` written by pyarrow 26 (min = max = 0.5): `select x <= 100.0 from read_parquet(f)` is TRUE for the NaN, `... where x > 100.0` counts 0 rows, `select max(x)` gives 0.5.
handling: A `Scan` reads each double column through `CASE WHEN isnan(x) THEN 'NaN' ELSE x + 0.0 END`, which DuckDB keeps no statistics for (#173). Setting `can_have_nan := true` on `read_parquet` might replace the `isnan` rewrite; that is for the sverify owners to decide.

checked.note: reverse pass: float stats are trusted unless nan_count != 0 or can_have_nan (extension/parquet/parquet_statistics.cpp#L90-L117, #L518-L527; default false at extension/parquet/include/parquet_reader.hpp#L302). The docs state can_have_nan's default and effect (data/parquet/overview#parameters), so the default path is documented; test/sql/copy/parquet/parquet_nan.test#L14-L37 pins only can_have_nan := true
